articleTitle: NGC experience with audit of excitation system performance
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Generator Excitation Systems and Stability
abstract: Since restructuring of the UK electricity supply industry in 1990, technical specifications favoured by the previous vertically integrated industry structure have been replaced through a progressive move to functional performance based specifications. This is particularly true for power station generator excitation system performance. This paper briefly outlines the areas covered by the UK National Grid Company's (NGC's) functional specification and details NGC's experience in auditing excitation system performance and associated data.

articleTitle: Determination of excitation control system settings
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Generator Excitation Systems and Stability
abstract: The paper outlines the application of a pseudo-analytical technique to determine the parameters of a power system stabiliser (PSS) for a practical system. The basis of the technique is also applicable to AVR setting procedures.

articleTitle: An engineering strategy for the major refurbishment of excitation systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Generator Excitation Systems and Stability
abstract: A major refurbishment of the excitation systems of every generator unit in a power station may in itself be regarded as unusual, requiring a well planned strategy for implementation. Consider then if this was required at every major generating station on a power system. This is the situation presently being faced in Argentina where an intensive programme for the retrofitting of power system stabilisers is underway. This paper discusses the strategy being adopted by the various parties involved and makes the point that whilst it is governed to a large extent by conditions particular to the system itself, other external factors have combined to influence the approach adopted.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Generator Excitation Systems and Stability
abstract: The authors describe how Power Technologies, Inc. (PTI) designed the PSS/1 power system stabiliser to improve dynamic stability and undamped power angle oscillations. The stabiliser implements real-time software in a microprocessor-based system to produce supplementary stabilising signals to the excitation controls of any generator. The stabiliser has been applied to the existing controls on steam driven, hydro driven or pumped storage generation systems.

articleTitle: Design of a novel digital automatic voltage regulator
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Generator Excitation Systems and Stability
abstract: In the control of synchronous machines excitation, automatic voltage regulators (AVRs) have been used for many years. AVRs have evolved from the early electromechanical types to the solid state AVRs controlled with analogue circuits found most commonly in service today. With recent advances in microprocessor technology making faster and more powerful processors readily available it is now possible to implement more complex forms of adaptive and fixed parameter based controllers. However these more complex forms of control have some limitations and it will take more time to develop them into widely acceptable products. The conventional forms of control used in most digital AVRs are the same as in their analogue equivalents and hence no improvement in dynamic performance will result from a move to digital. However there are many advantages for both the customer and supplier in changing to a digital AVR. The digital AVR illustrated in this paper can be looked upon as equivalent in performance to the more sophisticated of the analogue AVRs available.

articleTitle: Experience with replacing rotating exciters with static exciters
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Generator Excitation Systems and Stability
abstract: Scottish Power and Scottish Hydro have completed the upgrade of the Anglo/Scottish interconnector from 850 MW to 1600 MW. This involved rebuilding the West Coast (Strathaven/Harker) line to allow one circuit to be operated at 400 kV (the other remained at 275 kV), and the installation of static excitation systems at Longannet and Hunterston power stations to improve generator stability under system fault conditions. This paper describes the installation and commissioning of the new excitation systems at Longannet.

articleTitle: Experience with excitation systems in National Power
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Generator Excitation Systems and Stability
abstract: Although their earlier types of excitation systems are performing reasonably well, there are more frequent problems appearing especially associated with the mechanical plant of National Power, UK, which although are not causing significant loss of generation, are causing increased operational costs and engineering. Company staff skilled in these areas are spending time on other project work and are becoming increasingly unavailable for attending breakdowns. Here, the author describes National Power's experience with their power station generator excitation systems.

articleTitle: A robust power system stabiliser for an overseas application
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Generator Excitation Systems and Stability
abstract: This paper presents a method of designing robust power system stabilisers (PSS) for damping low frequency electromechanical oscillations. The technique uses a quadratic cost function for specifying the closed loop performance and H/sub /spl infin// constraints for the closed loop robustness. The structure of the controller can be selected by the engineer thus allowing robust tuning of existing PSS. In addition, the upper and lower limits of the PSS are incorporated thus ensuring that the recommended parameter values can be implemented. A sequential quadratic algorithm is used to solve the optimisation problem. The method is implemented on an equivalent of the Eskom network and the results are discussed. The proposed method of tuning the PSS is shown to be superior to the conventional techniques both in performance and robustness properties. An important consequence of the approach is that existing PSS can simply be retuned for optimal robust performance without replacement of the generator excitation control equipment.
